requirement.original: 文件和图片顶部宽度和左右宽度仍然不统一。此外文件太大了无法上传并且没有报错
requirement.clarified: Two bugs in the message-composer attachment tray: (1) file and image thumbnail chips have inconsistent bounding-box geometry (overlay offset by 4px, strip padding asymmetric); (2) when a file exceeds the 10 MB upload limit the user sees no error — the silent-return path discards the file without feedback, and even if a network-error 413 occurs the send path silently removes the failed attachment without alerting the user.
requirement.what: Unify attachment chip layout (single THUMB_SIZE constant, overlay at left:0, consistent padding); surface upload failures via Modal.alert at pick time and block send when error-state chips exist
requirement.why: Users cannot tell when an attachment silently fails; the layout inconsistency between file and image thumbnails is visually jarring and reported as a regression from an expected unified design

included: Layout: THUMB_SIZE constant unification, overlay left:0, strip padding normalization
Error surfacing: Modal.alert at pick-time size check (3 callsites)
Send guard: block send when any attachment has status=error
Translation keys: session.attachmentTooLarge, session.attachmentUploadFailed in all 9 languages

success_criteria: Image chip and file chip render identical bounding boxes; overlay flush at left:0
Picking a file > 10 MB shows Modal.alert immediately; chip NOT added to tray
Attempting to send with error-state attachment shows Modal.alert and blocks send
Successful upload flow (ready attachment) behaves identically to before
constraints: Modal must be imported from @/modal, not Alert from react-native
Translation keys must be added to all 9 language files (en, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ru, pl, es, ca, it, pt, ja)
MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES value (10 MB) must not change
useAttachments hook should not import UI-layer Modal directly — prefer callback or HappyError throw pattern

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Attachment chip thumbnails have inconsistent visual framing (overlay offset, unequal padding for image vs file types); file-too-large and network-error upload failures show no user-facing error
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: Bug 1: Commit f6f129a1 changed strip padding from paddingHorizontal:12/paddingVertical:6 to padding:12 and changed overlay.left from 0 to 4, creating an overlay-thumbnail misalignment. No shared THUMB_SIZE constant was defined at creation time. Bug 2: All three attachment pick paths (pickImage, pickDocument, addFileFromPaste) perform a silent `return` when size > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES with no Modal.alert. The send path in useComposerSend treats hasAttachments as `attachments.length > 0` (includes error items) and silently drops them via clearAttachments() without user notification.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: f6f129a1 — Auto-commit: 2026-03-25 12:27:02 (introduced overlay.left:4 and padding:12); f8b208fa — initial attachment implementation (silent-return pattern present from day 1)
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: The padding change in f6f129a1 was likely an automatic style normalization. The silent-return pattern in the initial commit f8b208fa was a deliberate but incomplete implementation — error surfacing was deferred.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: overlay.left:4 misaligns the loading/error overlay with the thumbnail it covers. The silent-return on oversize means the user gets no feedback and may not understand why their attachment was not sent.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Silent return: since 2026-03-23 (f8b208fa). Layout regression: since 2026-03-25 (f6f129a1).

development_approach.validation_approach: QA must: (1) render the attachment tray with both an image and a file chip and measure/observe that their frames are identical, overlay is flush; (2) pick a file > 10 MB and confirm Modal.alert appears without adding a chip; (3) trigger a network-error upload (mocked or actual oversize via server path) and confirm error chip remains in tray then attempt send — confirm Modal.alert blocks send; (4) verify successful upload flow still sends with attachment. Must test both desktop (1280x720) and mobile (390x844) viewports.
